accepted.question: Explain the Chinese Wall model by stating the conflict it is designed to resolve, its classification as a policy type, the condition under which a subject may be granted access to an object, and the two conditions that must hold before write access is permitted.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy was proposed by Brewer and Nash to address conflicts of interest.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash (1989) proposed a policy called the Chinese Wall Policy that addresses such conflicts of interest.

marking_points.point: It is classified as an access control confidentiality policy rather than an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: Under the simple security rule, a subject may access an object only if that object lies within the same company datasets already accessed (within the Wall).
marking_points.quote: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s,
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote states the access condition that the object must be in the same company datasets already accessed by the subject, matching the marking point.

marking_points.point: Alternatively, access is allowed if the object belongs to a completely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that access is allowed when the object belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class, matching the marking point.

marking_points.point: Write access is allowed only when the simple security rule permits it and no readable object in a different company dataset holds unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

questions.question: Describe six (6) aspects of the security mechanisms found in Windows systems, covering the overall mechanism set, access control, subjects and credentials, access rights, directory services, and the risks arising from complexity.

marking_points.point: Windows provides complex mechanisms covering user account management, object management and access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control in Windows allows fine-grained control over diverse entities both in the OS and in applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: In Windows, subjects are processes and threads, and their security credentials are kept in a token.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: Access rights in Windows are encoded as a 32-bit mask and include standard rights such as DELETE and WRITE_DAC.
marking_points.quote: Encoded as a 32-bit mask

marking_points.point: Active Directory, introduced in Windows 2000, is an LDAP-like directory service that organizes users, groups, credentials, resources and security policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: The complexity of Windows security is a weakness because misconfiguration and implementation bugs can cause severe security incidents.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

questions.question: Discuss six ways in which malware attacks and propagates through a computer system, referring to the techniques malware uses to spread, hide, and affect the infected host.

marking_points.point: Malware can propagate by self-replication, with programs copying themselves to improve their chances of survival.
marking_points.quote: To increase their survival chances, programs can replicate themselves

marking_points.point: A virus can spread through boot sector infection of distributed media, as demonstrated by early malware included in the boot sector of software diskettes.
marking_points.quote: Included in a boot sector of distributed software diskettes

marking_points.point: A worm can propagate remotely by exploiting a debugging feature that allows remote execution, as the Morris worm did across the Arpanet.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: An executable virus can attach its body to a legitimate program so that the infected file carries the malicious code.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: A rootkit hides malicious processes and software so that the infected machine remains under the control of the malware author.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware steals user credentials and records activity such as keystrokes and visited sites, which can lead to identity theft.

questions.question: Discuss the Samy worm as an example of a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack, covering how the malicious script was injected, how it spread between users, and the scale of the resulting infection.

marking_points.point: It retrieved the victim's list of friends (heros) by issuing a GET request to a user profile.

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile had their own profile and friends list infected, enabling self-propagation.

marking_points.point: The infection ultimately reached approximately one million MySpace profiles.

marking_points.point: The attack exploited the fact that any web application returning unfiltered user input is a potential XSS vulnerability.
